title: Mar Zutra of Drishba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Bava Batra 126b relates that he was a firstborn who divided a basket of pepper equally with his brothers. He came before Rav Ashi, who told him, “Since you have waived your right in part, you have waived it with respect to all the property.” The commentator Hyman cites as R. G. explains the name as a place-name. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads Mar Zutra Rushba.

notes.text: The commentator printed ר״נ has not been securely identified. The complete ending, including the Rushba variant, is restored in English.

The earlier finite Vilna Rashbam126b nonmatch and later Goldschmidt search lead do not identify Hyman’s ר״נ. No new whole primary commentary was supplied or read here, so neither Rabbenu Nissim nor Rashbam is silently expanded. The firstborn’s equal basket division concerns waiver of his extra share in Hyman’s account; the precise place-name claim remains attributed to the unidentified commentator. Dikdukei Soferim’s Rushba remains Hyman’s reported reading, with the complete ending preserved rather than the old truncated English.

Hyman’s printed page reads ר״ג where the supplied transcription has ר״נ. A matching gloss, transmitted under Rabbenu Gershom, explains מדרישבא as a place-name. The directly consulted Bava Batra 126b reads Mar Zutra mi-Drishba. In Dikdukei Soferim, Bava Batra p. 350, note 9, the printed-text column retains that form and the manuscript column gives Mar bar Rushba. Hyman’s abbreviated report is distinct from the apparatus’s fuller wording. The waiver concerns the firstborn’s additional share.
